_note: CURATION REQUIRED. Every neighborhood whose value is null has NO verified stock photo yet and must be curated by hand before it can be used.

Only entries with a non-null value have been verified: each one was checked on its Unsplash photo page and the 'verified_location' field below quotes the location the photographer actually recorded on that photo.

Entries were deliberately left null rather than filled with search-result guesses. Unsplash keyword search is NOT location proof - a top result for 'fremont seattle' turned out to be a photo of Portland, Oregon. A wrong photo ID yields a broken image or a picture of the wrong city, which is worse than no image.

To curate an entry: open the Unsplash photo page, confirm the photographer set a location inside that neighborhood (or the subject is an unmistakable landmark of it), then record url + description + source_page + verified_location in the same shape as the curated entries.
'description' is used verbatim to build alt text, so write it as a complete sentence ending in a period. The pipeline appends the 'illustrative image' disclaimer itself - do not include one here.

ATTRIBUTION: Unsplash asks that the photographer be credited. Photographer names were not captured during verification, so add a 'photographer' field from each source_page before these images are published.
A value may be either a plain URL string or an object with a 'url' key. null means uncurated and makes the pipeline fall back to the 'default' entry.
